data.body:
## rebar-debug final report — RESOLVED, merged

**Gerrit:** https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/1502 — LLM-Review +1, Verified +1,
submitted, MERGED (patch set 3).

**Proven root cause.** See the RCA comment above. In one line: the `else` in
`hi = line_end if line_end and line_end >= lo else len(lines)` served two disjoint inputs — the
documented `line_end == 0` sentinel and a malformed inverted range — so the latter silently
became "read to EOF".

**Test.** `tests/unit/test_pai_tools_read_file_range_4c2b.py`, 9 cases: four inverted shapes
(including the reported 115/30 and a negative `line_end`), an inverted range on a file too short
to contain either bound, both `line_end=0` forms, an ordinary window, and the
`line_start == line_end` boundary. The 5 defect cases were confirmed RED for the right reason
before any fix existed; the 4 regression pins passed from the start (they encode unchanged
behaviour, which is the point of pinning them). Held out from the fix subagent — moved out of its
tree, path pattern declared off-limits — and GREEN after. Mutation check: re-seeding the exact
guard (`line_end if line_end and line_end >= lo else …`) returned the 5 defect cases to RED and
left the 4 pins green; restoring the fix returned all 9 to green. Re-run after the
comment-hygiene amendment, with the same result.

**Fix.** `src/rebar/llm/pai_tools.py`: a module-level `_resolve_read_window(line_start, line_end)`
returns the clamped inclusive `(lo, hi)` window and raises `ValueError` for a malformed range;
`read_file` calls it inside its existing `try`, so the message surfaces through the already-present
`except ValueError -> f"Error: {exc}"` path and no new error-handling branch is added. The check
runs **before the file is opened**, which is what makes the rejection a property of the request
rather than of the file — an inverted range past the end of a 2-line file reports the same error
instead of `(empty range)`. The extraction also makes `line_end == 0` the sentinel's only
meaning, which is what it always was: the `>= lo` clause was the conflation. The malformed-range
rule is stated in `read_file`'s own docstring, because Pydantic AI hands that docstring to the
agent as the tool contract.

**Scope & safety.** Caller-dependency sweep: `read_file` is a closure handed to Pydantic AI
agents; its only in-repo references are the tool-name memoization set (`agent_call.py`), the
prompt text describing it (`operations.py`), and reviewer prompt docs. Nothing branches on the
return shape and nothing depended on an inverted range meaning EOF. One behaviour ordering
change worth noting for reviewers: for a call that is BOTH out-of-root/denied AND inverted, the
range error now wins over the path error — both are `Error:`, no content leaks, and the range
message names no path. The fix restores the tool's stated contract rather than creating
capability, adds no dependency, and weakened no existing test (the diff is one new module-level
helper plus a docstring; the only pre-existing lines removed are the three the helper replaces).

Two repo gates shaped the change and are worth recording:
* the shrink-only C901 ratchet (`.github/complexity-baseline.json` freezes
  `pai_tools.py::filesystem_tools` at 28). The first form of the guard took it to 29. Rather
  than raise the ceiling or suppress the rule, the window resolution was extracted to module
  level, which removed two decision points and added none — landing back at 28.
* the comment-hygiene gate rejected a bare commit sha in the new test's docstring; it now cites
  the sibling bug by ticket id, per the gate's own remedy text.

**Siblings.**
- *Construct axis:* the class is "a sentinel/fallback branch whose guard also swallows a
  malformed input". Swept every fallback in the two tool modules: `read_file`'s
  `or "(empty range)"` (honest — the range was read and is empty), `list_directory`'s
  `or "(empty)"`, and `search_files`' two `or "(no matches)"` (fixed under bf31). Probed the
  live tools rather than reading them: `list_directory` on a file -> `Error: [Errno 20]`, on a
  missing path -> `Error: [Errno 2]`; `read_file` on a directory -> `Error: [Errno 21]`, on a
  missing path -> `Error: [Errno 2]`. No siblings.
- *Parity axis:* the rule is "a read-only agent tool must report a request it cannot perform
  rather than answering as if it had performed it". Channel census over every tool this module
  hands an agent: `read_file` (fixed), `list_directory` (holds, probed above), `search_files`
  (holds, bf31), `show_ticket` and `comment_ticket` (both wrap the call in
  `except Exception -> f"Error: {exc}"`), `resolve_symbol` (returns `UNRESOLVED`, but discloses
  it — its docstring tells the agent verbatim that UNRESOLVED "is NOT proof it does not exist",
  and the error path names the exception; a documented fail-open, not a silent substitution),
  `mcp_toolsets` (documents "a malformed entry is a clear error, never a silent tool-less run").
  No MISSING slots.

**Residual risk.** None observed beyond the above.

**Replication.** The report's exact call shape, against a real repo file on the merged tree:
`read_file("src/rebar/llm/pai_tools.py", line_start=115, line_end=30)` now returns a 145-char
single-line `Error: inverted line range: line_end=30 is below line_start=115 (effective start
115). Pass line_end >= line_start, or line_end=0 to read to EOF.` — where it previously returned
the ~11,000-char read-to-EOF blob. A legitimate window (30..40) still returns 11 lines, and
`line_end=0` from line 1 still returns the whole file.
